evidence.interpretation: The actual List instance selects the direct helper from the runtime Applicative instance; Option-only laws cannot be assumed to reach this path. The fallback temporary input buffer has different ownership from an output accumulator inside G.

The separate unorderedTraverse path uses immutable Map accumulation with CommutativeApplicative and runtime StackSafeMonad checks. This closes the sibling-path inspection gap; do not apply a noncommutative List effect as a lawful Map traversal instance.

claims.rule: Do not share a mutable output builder across branches of a generic effectful traversal; retain immutable per-branch accumulators and deliberately exercise the optimized runtime branch.
claims.applicability: PR 4498, 2023-2024: the demonstrated failure is repeated continuation use in List-like branching, not a proven concurrent race. StackSafeMonad is a branch condition, not evidence of single-shot evaluation.
claims.counterexample: A strict local builder consumed before entering any effect can be safe. A fake marker instance is a targeted reproducer, not a production recommendation to advertise List flatMap as stack-safe.

claims.rule: Use mutable state inside mapAccumulate helpers only for known strict, ordered maps; for composition, thread each inner final state through the outer traversal and test both final state and transformed values.
claims.applicability: Observed accepted specialization boundary in PR 4209, 2022. Seq/IndexedSeq interfaces alone do not establish strictness; applying the same optimization today requires a fresh contract check.
claims.counterexample: Local mutation in a proven strict List map is not the same as mutable accumulation inside an arbitrary branching effect; a blanket ban on all vars would reject the accepted implementation.
